findings.title: Stop discarding ErrMissing in exported LoadOrDefault
findings.whyItBreaks: LoadOrDefault calls Load and drops the error signal (`v, _ := Load(key, m)`) at src/store.go:16. Load reports a missing key via ErrMissing (src/store.go:10), so previously callers could branch on `errors.Is(err, ErrMissing)`; LoadOrDefault now returns "" for both a missing key and a key that is present with an empty value, forcing every caller to conflate failure with a real value. It is also impossible to supply any default other than the zero value, contradicting the `OrDefault` name. This is an exported API, so the unusable contract is a present defect even with no in-repo callers.

findings.title: LoadOrDefault swallows ErrMissing, conflating absence with empty
findings.whyItBreaks: Load (src/store.go:7) returns the sentinel ErrMissing specifically so callers can tell a missing key from a present one; the new exported LoadOrDefault (src/store.go:15) discards that error and returns "" via `v, _ := Load(key, m)`. Because "" is itself a valid stored value in map[string]string, the new zero-value fallback is indistinguishable from real data. Trigger D applies: this is an exported/public swallow site, so the unusable contract is the defect even with no in-repo callers yet — every eventual caller is forced to treat a failed lookup as a legitimate empty string, and any caller that persists, reports, or acts on that value will act on a fallback as if it were real.

findings.title: Make parse_positive_int reject non-positive values or rename it
findings.whyItBreaks: The renamed carrier `parse_positive_int` promises a positivity guarantee, but the unchanged body `return int(value)` performs no validation: it accepts `0`, negative ints, negative numeric strings, floats, and bools. Callers that trust the name (charge() at src/validators.py:6 multiplies the result by 100; total_cents() at src/validators.py:11 sums those charges) will silently compute negative/zero charges and totals instead of failing fast, e.g. parse_positive_int("-5") -> -5 -> charge -> -500. The old name `read_int` made no such promise, so this misleading contract is introduced by this change.

findings.title: Lenient candidate parse silently drops real findings
findings.whyItBreaks: The changed line parses the first Codex (candidate) pass with normalizeReview(..., false). In lenient mode normalizeReview maps every raw finding through normalizeFinding inside a try/catch and filters the null results out of the findings array instead of failing. normalizeFinding throws on any missing required field (file, title, whyItBreaks, suggestedFix), invalid severity/category, bad lineStart/lineEnd, or non-P3 confidence < 0.7 — exactly the LLM output slop this tool routinely emits. So a real P1/P2 finding with one malformed required field is silently removed before the critic runs. The guard at src/core/review.ts:30 only rejects when summary is missing or checked is empty; checked is populated independently, so the pipeline proceeds with an empty/partial findings list. The critic receives that JSON at src/core/review.ts:35 and is prune-only (prompts/critic.md: 'Never add new findings'), so it cannot recover the dropped finding; deriveVerdict then returns pass for the emptied finding set — a false PASS on a PR with a real defect. Previously (strict default = true) the same malformed finding threw loudly out of review(), so failure was distinguishable from a legitimately empty findings list.

findings.title: Parse candidate findings strictly so malformed output fails loudly
findings.whyItBreaks: The added `false` argument selects normalizeReview's non-strict mode for the candidate pass (the project's schema module declares `normalizeReview(raw, strict = true)`, so omitting the arg — as the critic call on line 38 still does — means strict). In non-strict mode normalizeReview try/catches normalizeFinding per element and filters the null, i.e. a finding with a single malformed required field (missing whyItBreaks/suggestedFix, invalid severity/category, lineEnd < lineStart, non-finite line) is silently deleted instead of rejected. The only post-parse gate (src/core/review.ts:30) checks summary and checked only, so it does not notice; `candidate` is then serialized into the critic prompt (src/core/review.ts:35), and the critic is prune-only ('Never add new findings'), so the dropped finding can never reach the final result. If every finding is malformed, findings=[] and the review proceeds to a finding-free verdict. Previously the same malformed output threw out of review(), making failure loud and distinguishable; now a dropped finding is indistinguishable from a genuinely finding-free review.

findings.title: Rejecting parsed 0 silently overrides configured zero grace with default
findings.whyItBreaks: Substitution: value="0" -> guard `Number.isFinite(parsed) && parsed > 0` @src/shared/runner-process.ts:135 now REJECTS 0 -> returns fallbackMs. Consumer #1: RUNNER_TIMEOUT_GRACE_MS = readRunnerDurationMs(process.env.NEEDLEFISH_RUNNER_TIMEOUT_GRACE_MS, 5000) @src/shared/runner-process.ts:3-6, read as the SIGTERM->SIGKILL delay `}, RUNNER_TIMEOUT_GRACE_MS)` @src/shared/runner-process.ts:124; with env=0 the operator asked for an immediate hard kill but now gets a 5000ms wait. Consumer #2: RUNNER_SIGKILL_GIVE_UP_MS = readRunnerDurationMs(process.env.NEEDLEFISH_RUNNER_SIGKILL_GIVE_UP_MS, 2000) @src/shared/runner-process.ts:7-10, read as the give-up delay `}, RUNNER_SIGKILL_GIVE_UP_MS)` @src/shared/runner-process.ts:123; with env=0 the intended immediate give-up now waits 2000ms. The pre-change `>= 0` deliberately admitted 0 (setTimeout(fn,0) is valid and means 'no delay'), so a previously-valid, explicitly-set config value is now silently replaced by a much larger default with no error, changing how long a timed-out runner child lingers before it is force-killed.

findings.title: Don't silently override an explicit 0 grace/give-up config with the default
findings.whyItBreaks: Before this change `parsed >= 0` explicitly accepted 0, so NEEDLEFISH_RUNNER_TIMEOUT_GRACE_MS=0 gave an immediate SIGTERM→SIGKILL escalation and NEEDLEFISH_RUNNER_SIGKILL_GIVE_UP_MS=0 gave an immediate give-up. Line 135 now rejects 0 and returns fallbackMs (5000 / 2000, src/shared/runner-process.ts:3-10), so an explicit 0 is silently discarded and the timers at src/shared/runner-process.ts:123-124 wait the full default instead. Nothing downstream rejects 0 (the value is only used as a setTimeout delay), so no defect was being fixed by disallowing it; the change is a config regression for operators who set 0 to skip the grace period.

findings.title: Rejecting 0 silently overrides valid zero-duration env config
findings.whyItBreaks: Substituting the previously-valid value "0": readRunnerDurationMs("0", 5000) and readRunnerDurationMs("0", 2000) now take the reject branch and return the fallback (5000 / 2000) instead of 0. Those results feed the escalation timers RUNNER_TIMEOUT_GRACE_MS and RUNNER_SIGKILL_GIVE_UP_MS at src/shared/runner-process.ts:124 and :123. A user who sets NEEDLEFISH_RUNNER_TIMEOUT_GRACE_MS=0 (escalate to SIGKILL immediately) or NEEDLEFISH_RUNNER_SIGKILL_GIVE_UP_MS=0 (stop waiting immediately) is silently given a 5s / 2s delay. This is a real config-precedence regression: 0 is a meaningful duration for a delay, and it was honored before this diff; the new `parsed > 0` guard treats a legitimate value as invalid rather than only rejecting negatives/NaN.

findings.title: Forward bundle.focus/deep into large-mode map and deep passes
findings.whyItBreaks: reviewLarge runs whenever isLarge(bundle) is true (patch > 30000 chars or > 10 changed files, src/core/review.ts:30-31). HEAD removed `focus: bundle.focus` and `deep: bundle.deep` from `mapBundle` (deleted between agentsMd and `}`, was lines 89-90) and removed `.replace("{{FOCUS}}", bundle.focus ?? "(none)")` from the deep-prompt chain (deleted at was line 122). Now the map pass receives no `focus` field, so the documented focus-based hotspot ranking (prompts/map.md:37: 'If a `focus` field is set (not null), rank matching surfaces higher') can never trigger, and the deep pass renders deep.md with the literal `{{FOCUS}}` token still in it (prompts/deep.md:96: 'Focus: {{FOCUS}} ...') instead of the user's focus. `--focus`/`--deep` therefore silently become no-ops for every large PR, while reviewSmall still honors them because it JSON.stringifies the full bundle (src/core/review.ts:52-55).

findings.title: Keep focus plumbing in reviewLarge; dropping it ignores focus on large PRs
findings.whyItBreaks: For large PRs (patch > LARGE_PATCH_CHARS or > LARGE_FILE_COUNT files) reviewLarge builds the deep prompt from loadPrompt("deep.md"), which declares a `{{FOCUS}}` slot — that slot was previously filled via `.replace("{{FOCUS}}", bundle.focus ?? "(none)")`. This PR deletes that substitution AND deletes `focus: bundle.focus` / `deep: bundle.deep` from mapBundle. At head, `bundle.focus` is referenced nowhere in src/core/review.ts (`rg -n focus src/core/review.ts` returns only comment words), while reviewSmall still serializes the whole bundle (`JSON.stringify(bundle)`) so focus keeps working there. Net effect: the user-supplied focus is silently ignored for large PRs and the literal `{{FOCUS}}` template token is handed to the model — inconsistent with small-PR behavior and a regression versus base.

findings.title: Restore {{FOCUS}} substitution in deep-review prompt
findings.whyItBreaks: The deep-prompt template deep.md carries a {{FOCUS}} placeholder (that is why the removed `.replace("{{FOCUS}}", bundle.focus ?? "(none)")` line existed at head~1, review.ts). Removing the replacement leaves the literal token `{{FOCUS}}` inside every deep-review prompt and, more importantly, drops the caller's focus directive: `bundle.focus` is now read nowhere in reviewLarge (the mapBundle no longer carries it either, src/core/review.ts:83-89). Small PRs still pass the whole bundle through JSON.stringify (src/core/review.ts:52-55), so focus keeps working there — large PRs silently lose the user's focus guidance and get a stray placeholder token instead.
